about: hxq lint --fix of one rule over a fixture program, then the fixture and the files it started from both compiled and RUN (haxe --interp) with and without -D dflag: a fix must keep what the program prints. Seeded from the redundant-braces review (dangling else through a loop, #if regions, macro returns). D* must be refused, F* fixed.

invocations.name: D1
invocations.note: dangling else through a for body: must be refused

invocations.name: D2
invocations.note: dangling else through a while body: must be refused

invocations.name: D3
invocations.note: nested for in the loop body of an if with else: must be refused

invocations.name: D4
invocations.note: else-less if as a loop body, followed by a statement

invocations.name: D5
invocations.note: #if region statement inside an if branch

invocations.name: D6
invocations.note: an else present only under a define

invocations.name: F1
invocations.note: else-if chain whose every branch can go bare

invocations.name: F2
invocations.note: plain for body

invocations.name: F3
invocations.note: define-switched expression in both branches

invocations.name: F4
invocations.note: break in a loop body

invocations.name: F5
invocations.note: value tail of a block expression

invocations.name: F6
invocations.note: while with a call body

invocations.name: F7
invocations.note: if inside a switch case

invocations.name: F8
invocations.note: return and throw of define-switched values in a function

invocations.name: F9
invocations.note: return macro in a macro function called from main

invocations.name: G1
invocations.note: fmt with symmetric braces over a value-position try whose catch body is a switch expression: no ; may follow the switch inside the inserted wrap

invocations.name: RC1
invocations.note: repeated-cast over each form its review refuted or held: unbraced guard, write in a right side, loop back edge, write and call ahead of the first cast, two runs in one statement; the fix must keep what the program prints

invocations.name: RC2
invocations.note: repeated-cast must not put its local ahead of the statement declaring the operand: with an outer binding of that name it would compile and cast the wrong value

invocations.name: HC1
invocations.note: hoist-common-branch-tail over a plain chain, an else-if chain, an emptied final else and a branch that may return early, beside the forms it must leave: a loop body, a tail reading a branch local, a tail that exits; the fix must keep what the program prints

invocations.name: HC2
invocations.note: hoist-common-branch-tail on a chain whose kept statement before the shared outer tail is itself a chain with a shared tail: the outer rewrite lands first and the inner waits for the next pass, so no call vanishes

invocations.name: HC3
invocations.note: the same nested shape in the final else of the outer chain

invocations.name: HC4
invocations.note: hoist-common-branch-tail on an outer tail that ends in a chain with its own shared tail: the inner chain waits for the outer rewrite, so no call runs a second time

invocations.name: HC5
invocations.note: hoist-common-branch-tail on a chain written as a statement with its own semicolon, final else kept and emptied: the moved tail leaves no empty statement for the compiler to refuse

invocations.name: HC6
invocations.note: hoist-common-branch-tail on a chain followed by a comment before its own semicolon, block and line form, final else kept and emptied: the tail goes after the semicolon, the emptied form is left alone, and the program compiles and prints the same
